Article 58
In handling complaints as referred to in Article 54 letter a, the Regional Apparatus as referred to in Article 55 is granted the authority to handle victims of acts of violence against Women, based on information obtained through other sources.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Pekanbaru. 2. Regional Government is the Government of the City of Pekanbaru. 3. Mayor is the Mayor of Pekanbaru. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of the City of Pekanbaru. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region. 6. Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment of the City of Pekanbaru or other designation hereinafter referred to as the Office is the Regional Apparatus that carries out the duties and functions of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment affairs. 7. Head of the Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment of the City of Pekanbaru or other designation hereinafter referred to as the Head of Office is the Head of Apparatus whose scope of duties and responsibilities covers Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment affairs. 8. Community is individuals, Families, Groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 9. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 10. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 11. Every Person is an individual or corporation, whether in the form of a legal entity or not a legal entity. 12. Protection is all preventive actions, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of Women and Children from acts of violence. 13. Gender is a concept that refers to differences in roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 14. Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the implementation of gender and Child data consisting of regulatory components, institutions, and mechanisms in the Region in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of gender-responsive and child-sensitive development policies/programs/activities. 15. Selected Data is data selected according to sex and general. 16. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and Men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 17. Gender sensitivity or gender awareness is the ability to identify power relationship gaps between Women and Men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and Men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and Men are different. 18. Gender Mainstreaming in the region hereinafter referred to as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of regional development policies, programs, and activities. 19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of trafficking in persons. 20. Gender Equality hereinafter referred to as KG is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between Women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors. 21. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that Women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 22. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a Woman. 23. Empowerment of victims of violence is the strengthening of Women victims of violence to be able to try and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services. 24. Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons or hereinafter referred to as TPPO is any action or series of actions that meet the elements of criminal acts determined in Law Number 21 of 2007 Concerning the Eradication of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons. 25. Health rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and naturally in the family and in society. 26. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out social functions again properly. 27. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area where the violence occurred back to the area of origin of the person concerned. 28. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Integrated Service Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA is a Technical Implementation Unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for Women and Children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 30. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb. 31. Fulfillment of Children's Rights hereinafter abbreviated as PHA is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 32.

Article 52
Protection of women victims of violence is implemented through the provision of integrated services.

Article 102
The strengthening and development of institutions providing protection services for Women as referred to in Article 101 is intended so that cases of violence against Women can be handled with:
a. appropriate targeting;
b. innovation; and
c. professional handling, by skilled personnel who possess gender sensitivity or gender awareness.

Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 33. Child with Excellence is a Child who has commendable character, extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 34. Children's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 35. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children. 36. Safe House is a temporary residence or new residence designed under strict supervision and guard conditions for 24 (twenty-four) hours that is kept confidential in accordance with standards based on applicable provisions intended for Women and Children victims of violence. 37. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 38. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 39. Violence is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 40. Victim is a Woman and/or Child who experiences misery and/or suffering that occurs in the area of the City of Pekanbaru. 41. People with HIV/AIDS hereinafter referred to as ODHA are people who have been infected with HIV both at the stage of no symptoms and those who already have symptoms. 42. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is a series of standardized written instructions regarding various processes of government administration, how and when it should be done, where and by whom it is done. 43. Child-Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the Government, Regional Government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's Rights. Article Protection of Women is organized with the following principles:
a. respect and appreciation for Human Rights; b. justice and gender equality; c. non-discrimination; d. empowerment; e. best interests of women; f. protection; g. continuity and sustainability; h. openness; i. order; j. legal certainty; and
k. local wisdom. Article Protection of Children is carried out based on the principles of:
a. respect and appreciation for human rights; b. non-discrimination; c. best interests of the Child; d. respect for the Child's opinion; e. the right to live, grow, and develop of the Child; and
f. local wisdom. Article The purpose and objectives of this Regional Regulation are as the basis and guidelines for the Regional Government and stakeholders to:
a. fulfill the rights of Women and Children; b. protect Women and Children maximally, provide a sense of security and peace for Women and Children; c. prevent the occurrence of violence against Women and Children; d. empower Women; e. empower Women victims of violence; f. provide services to Women and Children victims of violence; g. provide protection to Reporters and Witnesses; h. maintain household integrity so that a harmonious family is realized; i. encourage the realization of quality families; and
k. increase the participation of non-governmental institutions to support regional efforts in providing protection to Women. Article The scope of this Regional Regulation includes:
a. obligations and Responsibilities of the Regional Government; b. rights of Women and Children; c. improvement of the quality of life of Women in the Region; d. protection of Women; e. family quality; f. fulfillment of Children's rights; g. special protection of Children; h. Gender and Child Data System; i. funding; j. participation of Parents, Family/Relatives and/or Community; k. monitoring and Evaluation; l. guidance and Supervision; and
m. prohibitions and sanctions.

Article 20
The Women's empowerment system aims to:
a. improve the quality of life of Women and Families;
b. increase the institutional capacity of Women's empowerment in the Region, including the development of its gender system; and
c. provide protection of Women's rights from various forms of violence and other discriminatory treatment.

Article 26
Curative efforts as referred to in Article 23 letter d are carried out by means of:
a. optimizing technical service units related to complaints of violence against Women;
b. providing adequate facilities and infrastructure for handling health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance; and
c. carrying out handling of victims of crime and violence quickly, precisely, and accurately by law enforcement officials.

Article 22
In order to realize the objective of increasing the institutional capacity for Women's empowerment in the Region, including the development of its gender system as referred to in Article 30 letter, shall be carried out through efforts:
a. establishment, development and capacity strengthening of Women's protection institutions, including complaint units for violence against Women and legal aid services;
b. improving the quality of human resources of managers;
c. strengthening the institutional capacity of PUG in the Region; and
d. strengthening and developing gender data systems.
Paragraph
Methods of Providing Protection of Women's Rights From Various Forms of Violence and Discriminatory Treatment

Article 166
The implementation of special protection for Children is carried out through:
a. prevention of violence against Children;
b. provision of services for Children requiring special protection through coordination of parties from government and non-government institutions in the Region; and
c. strengthening and development of service provider institutions for Children requiring special protection.

Article 51
Capital assistance by facilitating soft loans as referred to in Article 58 letter shall be conducted by means of:
a. approaching financing source institutions to provide assistance to Women victims of violence;
b. assisting in the provision of facilities and infrastructure; and
c. endeavoring to ensure that available cheap capital assistance is obtained by Women victims of violence.

Article 24
Promotive efforts as referred to in Article 23 letter are carried out by:
a. strengthening coordination mechanisms and work networks between service units in efforts to handle cases of violence;
b. providing Communication, Information, and Education (IEC) materials related to the prevention and handling of violence; and
c. conducting socialization, advocacy, and social campaigns in the context of the prevention and handling of violence.

Part Two
Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

Article 81
Legal enforcement services and legal assistance as referred to in Article 54 letter are actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against Women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

Article 72
The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 65 letter (huruf) aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators of violence or other parties related to the perpetrators of violence.

Article 89
Social reintegration as referred to in Article 54 is carried out in the context of reuniting Women victims of violence with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for Women victims of violence.

Article 179
Special Protection for Child victims of sexual crimes as referred to in Article 167 letter a is carried out through efforts:
a. education about reproductive health, religious values, and moral values;
b. social rehabilitation;
c. psychosocial assistance during treatment until recovery; and
d. provision of protection and assistance at every level of examination starting from investigation, prosecution, until examination in court proceedings.

a. conducting efforts to improve family quality to realize gender equality and the rights of Children;
b. providing services for families in realizing gender equality and the rights of Children; and
c. strengthening and developing institutions that provide family quality improvement services.

a. implementation of provision of services for families in realizing gender equality and Child protection in the regions;

c. provision of facilities and infrastructure for services for families in realizing gender equality and Child protection in the regions.

Strengthening and development of Women's Empowerment Service Provider Institutions in the Region as referred to in Article 50 shall be implemented by the Regional Government by undertaking the following matters:
a. establishing cooperation between Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women and Child empowerment with various partnership networks originating from the community, NGOs, foundations, universities, and other institutions engaged in the provision of Women's empowerment services in the Region;
b. endeavoring to ensure budget adequacy through proportional provision in the APBD and other non-binding sources based on laws and regulations; and
c. conducting approaches and embracing various structural and non-structural groups with the following backgrounds:
1. professional groups;
2. academics; and
3. community leaders,
to contribute to the institutional development of UPT PPA; and
d. conducting various trainings, technical guidance, workshops, FGDs, and other forms related to efforts to strengthen and develop Women's Empowerment Service Provider Institutions in the Region.

Article 103
The implementation of family quality improvement is carried out continuously.

Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 33. Child with Excellence is a Child who has commendable character, extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 34. Children's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 35. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children. 36. Safe House is a temporary residence or new residence designed under strict supervision and guard conditions for 24 (twenty-four) hours that is kept confidential in accordance with standards based on applicable provisions intended for Women and Children victims of violence. 37. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 38. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 39. Violence is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 40. Victim is a Woman and/or Child who experiences misery and/or suffering that occurs in the area of the City of Pekanbaru. 41. People with HIV/AIDS hereinafter referred to as ODHA are people who have been infected with HIV both at the stage of no symptoms and those who already have symptoms. 42. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is a series of standardized written instructions regarding various processes of government administration, how and when it should be done, where and by whom it is done. 43. Child-Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the Government, Regional Government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's Rights. Article Protection of Women is organized with the following principles:
a. respect and appreciation for Human Rights; b. justice and gender equality; c. non-discrimination; d. empowerment; e. best interests of women; f. protection; g. continuity and sustainability; h. openness; i. order; j. legal certainty; and
k. local wisdom. Article Protection of Children is carried out based on the principles of:
a. respect and appreciation for human rights; b. non-discrimination; c. best interests of the Child; d. respect for the Child's opinion; e. the right to live, grow, and develop of the Child; and
f. local wisdom. Article The purpose and objectives of this Regional Regulation are as the basis and guidelines for the Regional Government and stakeholders to:
a. fulfill the rights of Women and Children; b. protect Women and Children maximally, provide a sense of security and peace for Women and Children; c. prevent the occurrence of violence against Women and Children; d. empower Women; e. empower Women victims of violence; f. provide services to Women and Children victims of violence; g. provide protection to Reporters and Witnesses; h. maintain household integrity so that a harmonious family is realized; i. encourage the realization of quality families; and
k. increase the participation of non-governmental institutions to support regional efforts in providing protection to Women. Article The scope of this Regional Regulation includes:
a. obligations and Responsibilities of the Regional Government; b. rights of Women and Children; c. improvement of the quality of life of Women in the Region; d. protection of Women; e. family quality; f. fulfillment of Children's rights; g. special protection of Children; h. Gender and Child Data System; i. funding; j. participation of Parents, Family/Relatives and/or Community; k. monitoring and Evaluation; l. guidance and Supervision; and
m. prohibitions and sanctions.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Pekanbaru. 2. Regional Government is the Government of the City of Pekanbaru. 3. Mayor is the Mayor of Pekanbaru. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of the City of Pekanbaru. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region. 6. Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment of the City of Pekanbaru or other designation hereinafter referred to as the Office is the Regional Apparatus that carries out the duties and functions of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment affairs. 7. Head of the Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment of the City of Pekanbaru or other designation hereinafter referred to as the Head of Office is the Head of Apparatus whose scope of duties and responsibilities covers Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment affairs. 8. Community is individuals, Families, Groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 9. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 10. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 11. Every Person is an individual or corporation, whether in the form of a legal entity or not a legal entity. 12. Protection is all preventive actions, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of Women and Children from acts of violence. 13. Gender is a concept that refers to differences in roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 14. Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the implementation of gender and Child data consisting of regulatory components, institutions, and mechanisms in the Region in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of gender-responsive and child-sensitive development policies/programs/activities. 15. Selected Data is data selected according to sex and general. 16. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and Men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 17. Gender sensitivity or gender awareness is the ability to identify power relationship gaps between Women and Men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and Men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and Men are different. 18. Gender Mainstreaming in the region hereinafter referred to as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of regional development policies, programs, and activities. 19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of trafficking in persons. 20. Gender Equality hereinafter referred to as KG is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between Women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors. 21. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that Women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 22. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a Woman. 23. Empowerment of victims of violence is the strengthening of Women victims of violence to be able to try and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services. 24. Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons or hereinafter referred to as TPPO is any action or series of actions that meet the elements of criminal acts determined in Law Number 21 of 2007 Concerning the Eradication of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons. 25. Health rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and naturally in the family and in society. 26. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out social functions again properly. 27. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area where the violence occurred back to the area of origin of the person concerned. 28. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Integrated Service Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA is a Technical Implementation Unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for Women and Children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 30. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb. 31. Fulfillment of Children's Rights hereinafter abbreviated as PHA is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 32.

Article 22
In order to realize the objective of increasing the institutional capacity for Women's empowerment in the Region, including the development of its gender system as referred to in Article 30 letter, shall be carried out through efforts:
a. establishment, development and capacity strengthening of Women's protection institutions, including complaint units for violence against Women and legal aid services;
b. improving the quality of human resources of managers;
c. strengthening the institutional capacity of PUG in the Region; and
d. strengthening and developing gender data systems.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Pekanbaru. 2. Regional Government is the Government of the City of Pekanbaru. 3. Mayor is the Mayor of Pekanbaru. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of the City of Pekanbaru. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region. 6. Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment of the City of Pekanbaru or other designation hereinafter referred to as the Office is the Regional Apparatus that carries out the duties and functions of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment affairs. 7. Head of the Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment of the City of Pekanbaru or other designation hereinafter referred to as the Head of Office is the Head of Apparatus whose scope of duties and responsibilities covers Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment affairs. 8. Community is individuals, Families, Groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 9. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 10. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 11. Every Person is an individual or corporation, whether in the form of a legal entity or not a legal entity. 12. Protection is all preventive actions, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of Women and Children from acts of violence. 13. Gender is a concept that refers to differences in roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 14. Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the implementation of gender and Child data consisting of regulatory components, institutions, and mechanisms in the Region in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of gender-responsive and child-sensitive development policies/programs/activities. 15. Selected Data is data selected according to sex and general. 16. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and Men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 17. Gender sensitivity or gender awareness is the ability to identify power relationship gaps between Women and Men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and Men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and Men are different. 18. Gender Mainstreaming in the region hereinafter referred to as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of regional development policies, programs, and activities. 19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of trafficking in persons. 20. Gender Equality hereinafter referred to as KG is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between Women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors. 21. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that Women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 22. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a Woman. 23. Empowerment of victims of violence is the strengthening of Women victims of violence to be able to try and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services. 24. Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons or hereinafter referred to as TPPO is any action or series of actions that meet the elements of criminal acts determined in Law Number 21 of 2007 Concerning the Eradication of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons. 25. Health rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and naturally in the family and in society. 26. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out social functions again properly. 27. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area where the violence occurred back to the area of origin of the person concerned. 28. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Integrated Service Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA is a Technical Implementation Unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for Women and Children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 30. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb. 31. Fulfillment of Children's Rights hereinafter abbreviated as PHA is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 32.
